examples.title: Quick start
Your user struct

features: **Only what you use.** An app imports only the sign-in methods it offers, and a plugin of your own gets the same powers as the built-in ones: operations, hooks, columns on the user table, its own tables and migrations.

**Your database, your joins.** The auth tables sit beside yours. Read and join them with typed sqlb columns, so a renamed column is a compile error rather than a production bug. Only writes are closed, because the invariants live in Go.

**One pipeline for every entry point.** Each feature is one typed operation. A Go call, an HTTP route and a GraphQL resolver all run the same code, so none can skip the rate limit, the CSRF origin check, the session requirement or a hook.

**Security pinned by tests.** Constant-time comparison of every secret is a source guard that fails the build; one password hash on every sign-in path, known account or not, is a timing test; only verified identities ever match a person; tokens are single-use under concurrency.
**Three engines, one behaviour.** Values are normalized in Go and compared byte for byte, and one integration suite runs on Postgres, MySQL and SQLite.

**A dependency-free core.** The core module depends on the standard library and sqlb only, enforced by a test; argon2, WebAuthn and each framework adapter are separate modules you download only if you import them.
table:
| Package | What it adds |
|---|---|
| `plugin/email` | Email identities, verification links, change with undo, many addresses per user, sign-in codes |
| `plugin/password` | argon2id passwords, sign-up, sign-in, reset, change; `password/hibp` checks breaches; a separate module |
| `plugin/phone` | Phone identities, SMS codes, sign-in and sign-up with a code alone |
| `plugin/username` | Handles, reserved names, availability |
| `plugin/ldap` | Sign in with the username and password of an LDAP directory (OpenLDAP, Active Directory, FreeIPA, lldap), checked by the directory and never stored; TLS required, a replaceable `Directory`; a separate module |
| `plugin/siwe` | Sign-In with Ethereum (ERC-4361): a single-use nonce, the message checked against your site, chain and time window, several wallets per user, a replaceable `Verifier` for smart-contract wallets; a separate module |
| `plugin/oauth` | Google, GitHub, any OpenID Connect issuer; optional sealed provider tokens, refreshed before expiry |
| `plugin/twofactor` | TOTP, mailed or texted codes and security keys, several per user, with recovery codes; asked after password sign-ins by default (better-auth's rule), any other rule through `WithPolicy`; `RequireEnrolment` makes a factor mandatory through a session task |
| `plugin/passkey` | Passkeys (WebAuthn); a separate module |
| `plugin/emailchallenge` | Passwordless sign-in by one challenge a link and a code both complete, always signing in the browser that asked |
| `plugin/magiclink` | Sign-in by a single-use link to a verified address or number |
| `plugin/apikey` | API keys with scopes for scripts and integrations |
| `plugin/jwt` | Short-lived JWTs (EdDSA, RS256 or ES256) from a session, a JWKS, a Go verifier, and named templates shaped for another service (presets for Supabase, Hasura, Convex and Firebase in `jwtpreset`) |
| `plugin/admin` | Find and search users, ban and unban, revoke sessions, roles and permissions decided by a pluggable `Authorizer` (built-in admin and user roles; `plugin/access` roles, Casbin, OpenFGA or your own), impersonate (visible to the user, one hour at most) |
| `plugin/invite` | Invitation codes with usage tracking, optionally invite-only sign-up |
| `plugin/referral` | User-to-user referral codes and the steps that complete a referral; a separate module |
| `plugin/terms` | Record which terms version each user accepted; block until the current one is |
| `plugin/anonymous` | Guest sessions before sign-up, linked to the account by an app hook on every sign-in path |
| `plugin/lastlogin` | Remember how and when each user last signed in |
| `plugin/metadata` | Public, private and user-editable JSON metadata per user in a table of its own; admin routes decided by your authorizer |
| `plugin/sessiondata` | Per-session app data in a table of its own, removed with the session; the core carries the same data inline on `Session.Data` |
| `plugin/handoff` | Hand a session to a native app or another client with a three-minute single-use token |
| `plugin/captcha` | Turnstile, reCAPTCHA or hCaptcha before sign-up, sign-in and reset, or only when a rate rule asks for a challenge; fails closed |
| `plugin/pow` | Proof of work instead of a captcha: a rate or geo rule with the challenge action asks the client for a hashcash proof (`X-Pow-Proof`), with no third party |
| `plugin/stale` | Mail the owners of accounts nobody has signed in to for a year (configurable) and, if you ask for it, delete the ones that never answer; run from your scheduler with `auth maintain` |
| `plugin/organization` | Organizations, teams, members, invitations by email or any identifier kind matched only to verified addresses, roles decided by a pluggable `Authorizer`, an active organization per session, built-in, static and per-organization roles checked by permission, lifecycle hooks, verified email domains that invite, suggest or auto-join; `orgjwt` puts the active organization in a JWT; a separate module |
| `plugin/access` | Permission statements and the roles built from them (better-auth's `access`), used by the organization plugin, by the admin plugin through `accessadmin`, by API-key permissions through `accessapikey`, and by any app; a separate module |
| `plugin/audit` | An audit log of security events, filterable by type and organization, with each user's own history; any sink (a SIEM, a log pipeline) through `Sink` and `Querier`, and any operation mapped to an event type |
| `plugin/sso` | Enterprise single sign-on: OpenID Connect and SAML 2.0 identity providers registered at run time per organization or email domain; a separate module |
| `plugin/samlidp` | Your app as a SAML 2.0 identity provider for wikis, ticketing and vendor tools: metadata, SP-initiated and opt-in IdP-initiated sign-on, signed assertions; a separate module |
| `plugin/scim` | A SCIM 2.0 server, so Okta, Entra ID and other IdPs provision and deprovision users and groups; a separate module |
| `plugin/deviceauth` | The device authorization grant (RFC 8628) for CLIs and TVs; `oauthdevice` issues OAuth tokens through `oauthprovider` instead; separate modules |
| `plugin/oauthproxy` | Provider sign-in on preview deployments through production's callback; `oauthpopup` signs in from a popup for apps embedded on other sites; a separate module |
| `plugin/oauthprovider` | Your app as an OAuth 2.1 authorization server and OpenID Connect provider, for other apps and MCP servers; a separate module |
| `plugin/webhook` | Signed outgoing webhooks (Standard Webhooks) for user, session, identity and security events, with retries, dead letters, replay and an SSRF guard; `webhook/signature` verifies them; a separate module |
| `plugin/agentauth` | AI agents sign in with their own keys and act for a user under the capabilities the user granted (Agent Auth Protocol); a separate module |
